# Billing System Migration Rollout Plan
### 40,000 Users — Old and New Systems Running in Parallel

## Overview

This plan migrates 40,000 users from the legacy billing system to the new billing system using a phased rollout. Both systems remain live and operational throughout the migration, allowing rollback at any point prior to full cutover. The old system is **not** decommissioned as part of this plan — decommissioning is explicitly deferred to a separate, later initiative that begins only after the final migration phase has been stable in production for a defined soak period.

---

## Phase 1: Canary (0.5% — ~200 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed full integration testing in staging, including parallel invoice-generation reconciliation against the old system for at least 2 full billing cycles with 0 unresolved discrepancies; rollback procedure has been tested end-to-end in staging.

**Population:** Internal employee accounts and opted-in volunteer customers on simple (non-usage-based) pricing plans only.

**Duration:** Minimum 2 full billing cycles.

**Goals:** Validate core billing flows (invoice generation, payment capture, dunning) against real production data volume and edge cases at low blast radius.

---

## Phase 2: Early Adopters (10% — ~4,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completed its full duration with invoice accuracy ≥ 99.9%, payment failure rate delta vs. old system ≤ 0.1 percentage points, zero critical (Sev-1) incidents, and all Sev-2 issues from Phase 1 resolved or have documented mitigations.

**Population:** Randomly sampled users stratified across plan types (usage-based, tiered, annual, monthly) and geographies, excluding highest-value enterprise accounts.

**Duration:** Minimum 2 full billing cycles.

**Goals:** Validate system behavior across plan diversity and confirm support/ops tooling scales beyond the canary group.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability Ramp (40% — ~16,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completed its full duration with invoice accuracy ≥ 99.9%, customer-reported billing ticket volume no more than 1.2x the Phase 2 baseline rate, support team formally signs off on runbook readiness, and finance has reconciled Phase 2 revenue postings against the old system with < 0.05% variance.

**Population:** Broader general customer base migrated in weekly waves (e.g., 10% of total per week), prioritized by lowest account complexity first.

**Duration:** 4 weeks (weekly sub-waves), with a 48-hour bake period between waves before proceeding.

**Goals:** Prove the system at meaningful scale and load while retaining the ability to pause between waves.

---

## Phase 4: Full Migration (49.5% — ~19,800 users, remaining accounts)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 3 completed in full with invoice accuracy ≥ 99.9%, no open Sev-1/Sev-2 incidents, finance reconciliation variance < 0.05%, and explicit written sign-off from Billing, Finance, and Customer Support leads.

**Population:** All remaining accounts, including highest-complexity and highest-value enterprise accounts, migrated in prioritized batches with white-glove support for top-tier accounts.

**Duration:** 2–3 weeks.

**Note on decommissioning:** The old billing system remains fully running, read-accessible, and able to receive rollback traffic through the end of Phase 4 and for a mandatory 90-day parallel-run/soak period afterward. Any proposal to disable, delete, or decommission the old system is a **separate, subsequent phase (Phase 5: Legacy Decommission)** that does not begin until the soak period is complete and a dedicated go/no-go review has occurred. Phase 5 is intentionally out of scope for the user-migration rollout described above.

---

## Risks

RISK: Invoice miscalculation causes customers to be over- or under-billed | Run parallel shadow-billing reconciliation between old and new systems for every account before and during migration, with automated diffing and alerting on any mismatch | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Payment gateway tokenization mismatch causes failed or duplicate charges during cutover | Migrate and validate stored payment methods/tokens in a dry-run against the payment processor's sandbox before each phase, with dual-write reconciliation | Payments Platform Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing disputes and confusion during migration waves | Staff a dedicated migration support queue, publish customer-facing migration comms in advance, and staff up support capacity ahead of each phase per the ramp schedule | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Data migration script corrupts or drops subscription/entitlement data for a subset of accounts | Run migrations in idempotent, resumable batches with pre/post record-count and checksum validation, and keep the old system as source of truth until sign-off | Data Migration Engineer
RISK: Regulatory/tax compliance calculations differ between old and new systems, causing incorrect tax remittance | Engage compliance/tax team to audit new system's tax engine against old system outputs for all applicable jurisdictions before Phase 2 begins | Compliance Lead

---

## Halt Criteria (Automatic Rollback Trigger)

The rollout must be **immediately paused** and the affected batch rolled back to the old billing system if, at any point during a phase:

- **Invoice accuracy drops below 99.5%** (measured as correctly-generated invoices ÷ total invoices generated, sampled hourly) — the primary numeric halt threshold, or
- Payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds the old system's baseline failure rate by more than 0.5 percentage points over any rolling 24-hour window, or
- Any single Sev-1 incident occurs that is attributable to the new billing system.

A halt requires sign-off from the Billing Engineering Lead before the next phase or wave may resume.

---

PHASES: 4
